title: German lawmakers approve debt-laden 2027 budget
summary: German lawmakers voted on a federal budget which foresees €556 billion in spending. Elsewhere, the Left Party is hosting a summit on femicide and the BSW party conference starts in Dresden. DW has…

image.caption: German lawmakers are set to vote on a federal budget which foresees €556 billion in spendingImage: Michael Kappeler/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Germany's ‌lower ⁠house ⁠of parliament, the Bundestag, ​voted in favor ​a €556 ​billion ($610 ‌billion) 2027 ‌federal budget on ‌Friday, taking on additional debt to boost ​defense ​and infrastructure spending.
Total new borrowing will reach €210 ​billion, just short of the record €215.4 billion recorded in ​2021 ‌during the COVID-19 pandemic, according to budget figures.
Chancellor Friedrich Merz's government has vowed a push to strengthen Germany's core civilian infrastructure and rebuild ​its military after decades of underinvestment.
"It is right that we invest in the railways and ​in climate protection," said Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil in parliament on Friday. "It is right... that we invest in our security."

German core defense spending will increase from €82 billion to almost €110 billion. When additional spending from the special defense fund is also taken into account, total defense spending will pass €150 billion.
"We are putting up the ⁠money for ​defense so that Ukraine can defend its freedom," Klingbeil said. "No child born in Germany today should ever have to experience war again."
